These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Use to_money and ZERO for money math Coerce line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO rather than int 0 or float literals, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with snake_case codes Reject invalid invoice operations by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, using codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount" with repr() of the offending value.
texts.at-0004: Guard mutations on invoice.status == draft Mutating invoice operations must first check invoice.status != "draft" and raise BillingError("invalid_state", ...), matching issue_invoice in ledgerly/invoice.py.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency_key before validating state
item.content: Every money-moving or balance-changing operation (refunds, credits, payment/invoice changes) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it first: scan `ledgerly.audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching `idempotency_key` and return the original record without reapplying. Pass `idempotency_key` into the `audit.record(...)` call.

item.title: Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by

Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
